accepted.description: Always true when the status is 202.

account.description: Proton account name from the API probe. Empty on the CLI backend.

backend_ready.description: On the API backend: the sidecar answered. On the CLI backend: a binary was found on PATH.

checking.description: A login/version check is in flight (drives the Refresh spinner).

keyring_locked.description:
The system keyring is locked (or couldn't be read). The Proton session
may still be in it. This is not a sign-out: don't show the login form.

version.description:
Sidecar path or identity on the API backend; binary version/path on the CLI backend.
On probe failure this holds the error text shown on the sign-in page.

oneOf.description: Present for per-file operations; None for info/error/summary lines.

ActivityOp.description: A per-file operation, for rendering a rich activity table.

error.description:
Why a failed op failed. `None` for successes, and for failures recorded
by a build that predates this field.

message.description: A sentence. Passwords and codes are never included.

build.description: Commit the binary was built from, the same string `neutronsync --version` shows.

active.description: Operations currently in flight (rendered as live "uploading…" rows).

activity.description:
The feed is a deque in the engine. On the wire, and in the OpenAPI
schema, it is a JSON array.

signed_out.description:
The watch daemon has detected the proton-drive session is signed out.
Surfaced as a distinct "sign in to resume" banner instead of error spam.

AuthStep.description: The next sign-in step. `url`, `token`, and `methods` are present only when `step` is `need_human_verification`.

token.description: Proton human-verification token, not the API bearer token.

ConflictOutcome.description:
How the engine settled a file that changed on both sides. Serialises as
`kept_both`, `kept_local`, `kept_remote` or `skipped` (the HTTP API).

ConflictRecord.description: A settled conflict, as stored in `conflicts`.

Envelope.description:
Everything a client needs in one object. `rev` grows only when the rest
changed, so a client can tell a repeat from an update.

HeldDeletes.description: A pair whose deletions were held back, as stored in `held_deletes`.

local.description: Files that would have left this computer.

remote.description: Files that would have left Proton Drive.

tracked.description: Files the pair tracked when the deletions were first held.

files_deleted.description: Always false. Removing a folder does not delete a file on either side.

Settings.description:
The settings a server can use, in their TOML spelling. Every key is
optional on `PUT`; an unknown key is refused.

run_in_tray.description:
Desktop window preferences. Optional on `PUT`, returned on `GET`, and
stored in `[options]` so a later settings write does not drop them.

bearerAuth.description: API token on TCP, as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Required on TCP only when a token is configured. The unix socket does not use a bearer token. `GET /api/v1/health` never requires one.

info.description: The `/api/v1` contract served by `neutronsync serve` and the desktop tray. No field or endpoint is removed, and none changes its meaning. New optional response fields and new endpoints may be added; clients ignore fields they do not know. Request bodies refuse unknown fields. Bodies are JSON, at most 64 KiB. The prose contract is `docs/HTTP_API.md`.

Server-sent events (`text/event-stream`). Each event is named `state`. The `data` line is an Envelope: `rev`, `state`, `held`, `conflicts`, `auto_sync` (the newest 100 activity items). With nothing to report, the server sends an SSE comment `: keepalive` every 15 seconds. The stream ends when the server shuts down.
The process is up. No token, origin, or Host check.
